reason: E1 shows coherent nanoprecipitates can strengthen a soft magnetic alloy with minimal coercivity increase, supporting the core mechanism. E2 demonstrates that isostructural alloying in the specific MnNiSi-CoNiGe system yields a large magnetocaloric effect, establishing the baseline. However, no cited evidence supports that aging at ~550°C produces coherent nanoprecipitates in this specific alloy system, nor that the strengthening mechanisms or magnetic-domain-wall-pinning avoidance apply to MnNiSi-based materials; these are extrapolated from a different alloy class (CoFeNiTaAl HEA).
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can strengthen an alloy without significantly increasing coercivity
Isostructural alloying in (MnNiSi)1−x(CoNiGe)x yields a large magnetocaloric effect near room temperature
Aging at ~550°C can produce coherent nanoprecipitates in this alloy system
Nanoprecipitate strengthening mechanisms (dislocation impedance, microband refinement) apply to MnNiSi-based alloys
Coherent precipitates avoid magnetic domain wall pinning, preserving the magnetostructural transition
